machine_goal.description: Decompose the v43 Prism operating candidate into bounded temporal obligations without treating a static point observation, PR narrative, or fit-check geometry as mechanical acceptance.

subsystems.goal: Deliver one bottle to the controlled application position and prevent double-feed during the active cycle.

Establish and maintain controlled bottle restraint and a justified rotation/reaction-force path while label wrap is active; the v43 Prism-named parts are a candidate closure path, not a proven mechanism.
Present label media at the correct time and maintain a mechanically meaningful label-transfer relationship during wrap.
Release the completed bottle and preserve clearance from the head, guides, stops, and neighboring products across reachable release motion.
Provide supported, restrained mounting and a reaction-force path for the labeling and capture assemblies.
Identify, constrain, and evidence the v43 Prism candidate's closure motion and reaction path before it is treated as a capture mechanism.

obligations.description: Exactly one intended bottle is positioned at the application station before capture is authorized.
Index-stop behavior establishes product position and then releases without requiring a second product to enter the occupied station.
The physical subassembly that closes, guides, limits, actuates, or preloads bottle capture is identified from authoritative evidence.
Bottle restraint remains valid throughout capture and rotation rather than only at one fit-check pose.
Required contact/tangency between the bottle and the justified wrap mechanism remains valid for the required wrap interval.
A supported reaction-force and restraint path exists for wrap drive, support rollers, bottle contact, and mounting structure.
Capture and release movement are free of unacceptable whole-body interference across the mechanically reachable motion set, not merely at the recorded CAD pose.
The label lead and peel/presentation relation remain valid while the bottle is captured and wrap motion is active.
The completed bottle can leave without unacceptable collision with labeler, support geometry, index stops, or neighboring products across release motion.
Mounting, support, and restraint geometry are sufficient for the relevant operating loads and reaction path.
The exact mate/constraint chain identifies what constrains the Prism slider, links, and arms, and whether that chain can establish the required closure relationship.
The Prism candidate has an exact actuator identity, stroke, hard limits, and closure/opening endpoints sufficient to define its reachable envelope.
A supported reaction-force path is bound from the active closure elements through the reaction base and mounting structure; actuator force, preload, and compliance are separately evidenced.

interfaces.description: Transport provides one indexed bottle in the required application envelope before capture closure is requested.
Capture provides controlled bottle restraint and wrap contact for label transfer during the defined interval.
Label presentation provides an appropriately positioned label lead during the active wrap interval.
Capture may release only after the wrap interval completes and reachable motion clearance is established.
Release provides a clear station before a new bottle is admitted to the controlled cycle.
The Prism candidate may provide closure only after its constrained motion, limits, actuator/preload authority, and reaction path are bound.

events.description: The intended bottle is established at the indexed application position.
The justified capture mechanism has established required bottle restraint and contact.
Usable label media is present at the required presentation boundary.
The wrap drive is commanded only after capture and label-presentation guards are valid.
Required wrap motion is complete under an explicit measured or validated authority.
The controlled product release is commanded after completion and clearance guards are valid.
The prior bottle has cleared the controlled application envelope.
A future closure command is modeled as unresolved until the kinematic chain and authority are bound.

states.description: Free approach: a bottle approaches the controlled application cycle without any asserted capture relationship.
Capture beginning: one identified bottle occupies the indexed position and closure may be requested, but capture is not yet established.
Captured state: the bottle is under the capture/rotation subsystem's required restraint and motion relationship; current v42 evidence does not verify that relationship.
Label-transfer interval: label media must remain valid while the captured bottle receives the label; occurrence and duration remain unresolved.
Wrap-rotation interval: the wrap mechanism is active within the captured state.
The completed bottle is permitted to leave the controlled station.
Free exit: the controlled station is clear and a new product may be considered for entry.
A required transition failed to arrive within its bounded watchdog or an evidence contradiction requires a hold.

transition_guards.description: Product position and index-stop behavior establish one active bottle before capture closure.
Capture closure/actuation, restraint, reaction force path, and reachable clearance are established before wrap can begin.
A valid label presentation relationship exists before wrap motion is authorized.
Wrap completion has a bounded measured or validated authority before release is commanded.
Reachable release and neighbor clearance are established before the next product is admitted.

invariants.description: Bottle restraint remains valid throughout CAPTURE_AND_ROTATION, including the active wrap mode.
Required mechanical contact remains valid during the WRAP_ACTIVE interval rather than being inferred from a static clearance measurement.

Label-transfer and wrap-rotation intervals occur only within the captured state; a transfer associated with wrap overlaps the wrap-rotation interval and neither may begin before capture is established.
Clearance and interference acceptance applies across mechanically reachable capture and release states, not only the current v42 pose.
A second product is not admitted while CAPTURE_AND_ROTATION remains occupied.

hypotheses.description: A physical carrier, slide, pivot, actuator, or preload assembly owns bottle-capture closure but is not yet bound into the current v42 evidence model.
required_evidence: A no-mutation native read or OEM assembly/drawing map that binds the exact parent, closure input, allowed motion, limits, and reaction mount of the FITCHECK belt and both support rollers.

hypotheses.description: Capture contact depends on a compliant or preloaded element whose evidence and usable range have not been established.
required_evidence: An OEM source or no-mutation native feature read identifying the compliant element, its preload or force range, travel, retention, and reaction path at the FITCHECK capture station.

hypotheses.description: A static v42 fit-check pose alone establishes operational capture and rotation.
required_evidence: Only interval-wide evidence with an identified capture owner, required contact, restraint, and reachable-motion coverage could establish operational capture; a static pose, mate, zero distance, or local pass cannot do so.

hypotheses.description: A required capture mechanism exists in a nested configuration, feature, or external assembly boundary not represented by current top-level inventory.
required_evidence: An exact source-package or assembly-boundary map showing whether a nested configuration, feature, or external assembly owns closure and how it connects to the named FITCHECK belt and rollers.

hypotheses.description: A translating roller carrier or slide moves one or both support rollers to establish bottle capture.
required_evidence: A no-mutation mate/feature/DOF read or OEM assembly drawing that binds at least one named FITCHECK support roller to a translating carrier, including travel limits, closure input, and reaction mount.

hypotheses.description: A pivoting arm, lever, or carrier moves a support roller into controlled bottle capture.
required_evidence: A no-mutation native read or OEM drawing identifying the pivot axis, angular limits, linkage to a named FITCHECK roller, closure force source, and reaction path.

hypotheses.description: The driven wrap-belt assembly itself translates, pivots, or otherwise closes to establish bottle capture against the support rollers.
required_evidence: A no-mutation native read or OEM assembly/drawing map binding FITCHECK_DRIVEN_WRAP_BELT_5x160x93_V25-1 to a carrier or actuator and specifying its controlled motion, limits, drive relationship, and reaction mount.

hypotheses.description: A pneumatic cylinder or actuator provides capture closure force or commanded compliance at the v42 FITCHECK station.
required_evidence: An OEM BOM/drawing and a no-mutation live binding of the exact cylinder or actuator, rod, stroke, force, valve/control relationship, and attachment to a named FITCHECK belt or roller.

hypotheses.description: A spring or other compliant preload mechanism maintains capture force while accommodating bottle variation.
required_evidence: An OEM drawing/BOM or no-mutation native feature read showing the exact spring or compliant element, preload setting or force range, usable travel, retention, and reaction path in the v42 FITCHECK station.

hypotheses.description: Another explicit mechanically justified closure mechanism, outside the listed carrier, pivot, belt-motion, pneumatic, or preload classes, owns capture.
required_evidence: A precise OEM or no-mutation native source identifying the closure mechanism, its input, constrained motion or force path, limits, interface to the named FITCHECK parts, and affected reachable states.

hypotheses.description: The two fixed Prism guide rails and floating carrier slider may represent the primary guided closure degree of freedom.
required_evidence: Bilateral exact current-pose slider-to-guide-rail adjacency is admitted for V43_WRAP. Bounded motion/endpoint evidence is still required before any prismatic degree-of-freedom, permitted motion direction, or stroke claim.

hypotheses.description: The fixed actuator envelope may represent an actuator that drives the carrier slider, but the inventory does not identify an actuator, stroke, or attachment.
required_evidence: Exact actuator/source identity, provenance of the fixed actuator-envelope geometry, attachment relationship to the slider or another closure element, and authoritative or accepted deterministic stroke/limit data. The zero-mate full-chain observation does not bind actuator ownership.

hypotheses.description: The two links and arms may transfer slider movement into a bottle-facing closure or support-roller relationship; that linkage is not shown by the point inventory.
required_evidence: The current-pose physical adjacency chain is supported, but all seven slider/link/arm/roller targets returned zero incident active-assembly mates and zero mate variation values. An authoritative OEM/source kinematic definition or explicitly accepted deterministic mechanism derivation is now required before any slider-to-roller motion-transfer claim.

hypotheses.description: The fixed reaction base may carry closure reaction load, but attachment, load direction, actuator force, preload, and mounting capacity are unbound.
required_evidence: Exact structural/topology path from active closure elements to the reaction base or another fixed support, plus authoritative force/preload or deterministic load inputs. Direct Link-1 to reaction-base contact is already excluded at the recorded V43_WRAP pose by 1.25 mm positive clearance.

payload.source_limit: The source observation is point-only. This architecture projection does not add motion, contact, force, timing, or acceptance claims.

result.admitted_observation: At the recorded V43_WRAP point, the exact slider, Link-1, and Arm-1 targets each had zero incident active-assembly mates and zero mate-traversal errors.
result.interpretation_boundary: This weakens a conventional active-assembly mate-defined chain for the queried targets but does not disprove physical guidance, contact linkage, feature-level relationships, motion, force, or a wider mechanism.

result.admitted_observation: At the recorded V43_WRAP point, exact Link-1 to reaction-base minimum distance was 1.2499999999999734 mm and classification was clearance.
result.interpretation_boundary: This excludes direct contact for that exact pair at that pose only; it does not exclude a wider reaction path through rails, slider, actuator, arms, fasteners, other components, or other reachable states.

result.admitted_observation: At the recorded V43_WRAP point, the exact carrier slider was within contact/coincidence tolerance of both fixed guide rails. Each pair returned minimum_distance_mm=2.7755575615628914e-14, zero intersection bodies, and zero intersection volume.
result.interpretation_boundary: This supports bilateral physical adjacency consistent with a guided-slider interface at that exact pose only. It does not establish a prismatic joint, allowed DOF, motion direction, stroke, preload, force, reachable motion, timing, or mechanical acceptance.

result.admitted_observation: At the recorded V43_WRAP point, FITCHECK_PRISM_CARRIER_SLIDER_15x80x60_V43-1 returned 0 mm minimum distance and contact_or_coincidence_within_tolerance against both FITCHECK_PRISM_LINK_15x10x25_V43-1 and FITCHECK_PRISM_LINK_15x10x25_V43-2; both pairs had zero intersection volume.
result.interpretation_boundary: This supports current-pose slider-to-both-links physical adjacency and strengthens the linkage-transfer hypothesis. It does not establish joint type, numbered link-to-arm correspondence, allowed DOF, motion, stroke, actuator ownership, force/preload, interval behavior, or mechanical acceptance.

result.admitted_observation: At the recorded V43_WRAP point, FITCHECK_PRISM_LINK_15x10x25_V43-1↔FITCHECK_PRISM_ARM1_33p0824x10x5_V43-1 and FITCHECK_PRISM_LINK_15x10x25_V43-2↔FITCHECK_PRISM_ARM2_18p6806x10x5_V43-1 each returned 0 mm minimum distance with contact_or_coincidence_within_tolerance and zero intersection volume; the crossed pairs each returned 49.999999999999986 mm clearance.
result.interpretation_boundary: This supports the same-number link-to-arm current-pose adjacency pattern and excludes crossed current-pose adjacency at 50 mm. It does not establish joint type, allowed DOF, motion, stroke, actuator ownership, force/preload, arm-to-roller continuity, interval behavior, or mechanical acceptance.

result.admitted_observation: At the recorded V43_WRAP point, Arm-1↔Roller-1 and Arm-2↔Roller-2 each returned 0 mm contact/coincidence with zero intersection volume; crossed arm-roller pairs returned 40.00000000000001 mm and 41.854292187489904 mm clearance.
result.interpretation_boundary: Combined with admitted slider-link and link-arm observations, this supports a complete current-pose physical adjacency chain along two branches from slider to rollers. It does not establish a mechanism, bearing function, DOF, motion direction, stroke, actuator ownership, force/preload, interval behavior, or mechanical acceptance.

result.admitted_observation: All seven exact slider/link/arm/support-roller targets returned zero incident active-assembly mates, zero observed mate variation values, and no mate traversal or parentage errors at the recorded V43_WRAP point.
result.interpretation_boundary: This is negative evidence against the active assembly itself defining the proposed linkage kinematics. It does not prove a free DOF, intended motion, or mechanical invalidity. Static physical adjacency remains supported; mechanism motion remains KINEMATIC_STATE_UNRESOLVED.
